column1: The 21 Mandarin initials (声母) group by where in the mouth they're made. Name the 4 LIP (labial) initials.
column2: b　p　m　f

column1: Name the 4 TONGUE-TIP (alveolar) initials.
column2: d　t　n　l

column1: Name the 3 BACK-OF-TONGUE (velar) initials.
column2: g　k　h

column1: Name the 3 PALATAL initials (tongue flat & forward, lips spread; only before i/ü sounds).
column2: j　q　x

column1: Name the 3 FLAT-TONGUE sibilant (dental) initials.
column2: z　c　s

column1: Name the 4 RETROFLEX initials (tongue curled up & back).
column2: zh　ch　sh　r

column1: Which 6 initials are ASPIRATED (released with a puff of air)?
column2: p, t, k, q, c, ch (their unaspirated partners: b, d, g, j, z, zh)

column1: Give the unaspirated↔aspirated pairs (no puff ↔ puff).
column2: b↔p, d↔t, g↔k, j↔q, z↔c, zh↔ch

column1: What "helper vowel" do you add to say z/c/s and zh/ch/sh/r by themselves?
column2: A buzzing -i (e.g. zi, ci, si, zhi, chi, shi, ri) — NOT the "ee" sound

column1: Tongue position: contrast x vs s vs sh.
column2: x = palatal (flat, forward, smiling); s = flat dental tip; sh = retroflex (tip curled back)

column1: j, q, x can ONLY be followed by which kind of vowel?
column2: i and ü sounds (e.g. ji, qu, xian) — never a, o, u, e directly

column1: Why are b(o), d(e), g(e), j(i), z(i), zh(i) written with a vowel in parentheses in the book?
column2: The vowel is only a helper to pronounce the consonant aloud; the initial itself is just the consonant

column1: List the 6 SIMPLE (single-vowel) finals 韵母.
column2: a　o　e　i　u　ü

column1: Compound finals in the "a" group?
column2: a, ai, ao, an, ang

column1: Compound finals in the "o" group?
column2: o, ou, ong

column1: Compound finals in the "e" group?
column2: e, ei, en, eng, er

column1: Compound finals beginning with "i"?
column2: ia, iao, ian, iang, ie, iu (iou), in, ing, iong

column1: Compound finals beginning with "u"?
column2: ua, uo, uai, ui (uei), un (uen), uan, uang, ueng

column1: Compound finals beginning with "ü"?
column2: üe, üan, ün

column1: Name the four tones (+ neutral) and their contour.
column2: 1st ˉ high-level; 2nd ˊ rising; 3rd ˇ dip-down; 4th ˋ falling; plus neutral (no tone, light)

column1: Say "ma" in all four tones with meanings.
column2: mā 妈 mother; má 麻 hemp; mǎ 马 horse; mà 骂 to scold

column1: Tone change: when TWO 3rd tones come together, the FIRST becomes what?
column2: 2nd tone. e.g. 你好 nǐhǎo → pronounced níhǎo

column1: Tone change: a 3rd tone BEFORE a 1st/2nd/4th tone is pronounced how?
column2: As a HALF 3rd tone — it falls and does NOT rise back up

column1: Tone change of 不 (bù) before a 4th tone?
column2: Becomes 2nd tone: bú. e.g. 不去 búqù

column1: What tone is 不 before 1st/2nd/3rd tones, or standing alone?
column2: Stays 4th tone: bù. e.g. 不吃 bùchī, 不难 bùnán, 不好 bùhǎo

column1: Tone change of 一 (yī) before a 1st/2nd/3rd tone?
column2: Becomes 4th tone: yì. e.g. 一天 yìtiān, 一年 yìnián, 一起 yìqǐ

column1: Tone change of 一 (yī) before a 4th tone?
column2: Becomes 2nd tone: yí. e.g. 一个 yígè

column1: What tone is 一 when standing alone or counting?
column2: 1st tone: yī

column1: Tone-mark placement: which vowel gets the mark, by priority order?
column2: Priority a, o, e, i, u, ü — mark the first one present. If i and u are together, mark the LAST one (diū, huī)

column1: Spelling rule: when ü follows j, q, x, how is it written?
column2: As plain u → ju, qu, xu (the umlaut is dropped)

column1: No-initial syllables i / in / ing are written how?
column2: yi, yin, ying (add y). Other i-syllables: replace i with y (ian → yan)

column1: No-initial ü / üe / üan / ün are written how?
column2: yu, yue, yuan, yun (add y, drop the umlaut)

column1: No-initial "u" is written how? And other u-syllables?
column2: u → wu. Other u-syllables: replace u with w (uan → wan)

column1: When a syllable starting with a/o/e follows another syllable, what do you insert?
column2: An apostrophe between the two syllables. e.g. zhēn'ài 真爱 (true love)

column1: Finals iou, uei, uen — how are they written after an initial?
column2: Drop the middle vowel → iu, ui, un. e.g. 旧 jiù, 水 shuǐ, 困 kùn

column1: How is a retroflex (erhua 儿) ending marked in pinyin?
column2: Add r at the end of the syllable. e.g. 饭馆儿 fànguǎnr

column1: When is the first letter of pinyin capitalized?
column2: For proper nouns and at the start of a sentence. e.g. 美国 Měiguó; 我是美国人。Wǒ shì Měiguó rén.

column1: Basic stroke-order rules for writing characters (笔顺)?
column2: Top before bottom; left before right; horizontal before crossing vertical; outside before inside; close the box last
